chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Aqeeqa, the shaving, and the naming, asking which of these should be done first. He (peace be upon him) said: 'All of that is done in one time: shaving, slaughtering, and naming.' Then he mentioned what Fatima (peace be upon her) did for her children, then said: 'The hair is weighed and silver is given in charity equal to its weight.'

key_terms.التَّسْمِيَةِ: At-Tasmiyah: the naming of the child
key_terms.الْحَلْقِ: Al-Halq: the shaving of the newborn's head
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةِ: Aqeeqa: the ritual sacrifice offered for a newborn child
key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ ( عَلَيْهَا السَّلَام ): Fatima (peace be upon her): the daughter of the Prophet, whose practice is cited as a model
key_terms.يُوزَنُ الشَّعْرُ: Yuzan al-sha'ru: the hair is weighed

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order and method for performing Aqeeqa according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the Sunnah of Aqeeqa, emphasizing the simultaneity of shaving, slaughtering, and naming, while explicitly linking the ritual to the practice of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her) for the Prophet's grandsons. It further codifies the charitable act of weighing the newborn's hair and donating silver of equivalent value, a practice rooted in the Ahl al-Bayt's tradition. This narration underscores the spiritual significance of gratitude and purification in early childhood rites within Shia jurisprudence.
